topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the cancer lecture series and sets out the learning objectives regarding environmental exposures and carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer etiology, risk factors, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual framework of cancer causation by exploring the interplay between genetic mutations, endogenous cellular processes, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens and viral infections contribute to cancer development, illustrated through the multi-factorial etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens induce direct DNA damage and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanistic summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic promotional mechanisms, host developmental susceptibility windows, and synthesize the broader concepts of cancer causation.

topics.label: Methodologies for assessing carcinogenicity and mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect and prove the carcinogenicity of environmental exposures.

topics.label: Closing remarks on risk-benefit assessment in cancer prevention
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with framing remarks on evaluating practical trade-offs between carcinogenic risks and everyday benefits.
